parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Find $\frac{dx}{dt}$ when the radius of the rod is 2 cm, giving your answer to 3 significant figures.
(4)

parts.label: b

(b) Find the rate of increase of the volume of the rod when $x=2$.

questions.stem: A curve has equation $3x^2-y^2+xy=4$. The points $P$ and $Q$ lie on the curve. The gradient of the tangent to the curve is $\frac{8}{3}$ at $P$ and at $Q$.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Use implicit differentiation to show that $y-2x=0$ at $P$ and at $Q$.
(6)
parts.mark_scheme: (a) $3x^2-y^2+xy=4$ (eqn *). Differentiates implicitly to include either $\pm ky\frac{dy}{dx}$ or $x\frac{dy}{dx}$ (ignore $(\frac{dy}{dx}=)$) M1; $6x-2y\frac{dy}{dx}+\left(y+x\frac{dy}{dx}\right)=0$: correct application ( ) of product rule B1; $(3x^2-y^2)\to (6x-2y\frac{dy}{dx})$ and $(4\to 0)$ A1; $\left\{\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{-6x-y}{x-2y}\right\}$ or $\left\{\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{6x+y}{2y-x}\right\}$ not necessarily required. $\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{8}{3} \Rightarrow \frac{-6x-y}{x-2y}=\frac{8}{3}$: substituting $\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{8}{3}$ into their equation M1*; giving $-18x-3y=8x-16y$; giving $13y=26x$: attempt to combine either terms in $x$ or terms in $y$ together to give either $ax$ or $by$ dM1*; Hence, $y=2x \Rightarrow y-2x=0$: simplifying to give $y-2x=0$ AG A1 cso [6]
